metaDescription: Six Bluetooth key finders compared on phone support, ring volume, water rating and battery, from Find My tags to Tile, to help you pick one for your phone.
introParagraphs: A Bluetooth key finder rings when you are close and lets passing phones report its last known spot when you are not. That makes it a better fit than a basic beeper for keys that follow you out of the house. The catch is that each tag is tied to a specific phone network, and picking the wrong one is the most common mistake.

We evaluated six Bluetooth key finders based on product specs and buyer feedback. Two are cross-platform Chipolo tags, one is the Life360 Tile with its own app, and three, the AirTag, UGREEN FineTrack and Qylara, are built for iPhone only. We compared stated ring volume, battery plan, water rating and the phones each one supports.
Decide on the phone first, then use the tables to match battery style and ring volume to how you carry your keys.

products.badge: Best Colorful Tag for Any Phone
products.name: Chipolo POP Tracker Tag, iOS and Android
specs: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

specList.label: Network
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

products.description:
The Chipolo POP is a Bluetooth key tag that works with either iPhone or Android, which is rare among tags. It uses Apple Find My on an iPhone or the Find Hub network on Android, so a household with mixed phones can buy the same tag. The listing states a loud ring of up to 120 dB, and the body comes in bright colors that are easy to spot on a dark table.

It has a built-in keyring hole, so no accessory is needed to hang it on house or car keys. For keys that leave the house, the global network behind your phone shows a last known location on a map. A single tag runs on one network at a time, so two people on different phones each need their own tag. The listing mentions a 2 year warranty with replacement handled through the seller.

The listing does not give a water rating or battery type, so we do not state either. Compared with the Chipolo Loop at up to 125 dB it is slightly quieter and has no rechargeable cell stated, and against the AirTag it does not offer step by step directions to a lost item.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants one attach-and-go tag that works with iPhone or Android.

cons: No water resistance rating appears in the listing
Battery type and life are not stated in the product text

products.name: Apple AirTag (2nd Generation), 4 Pack
specs: Precision Finding on iPhone and Watch

specList.label: Directions
specList.value: Precision Finding on iPhone and Apple Watch

products.description:
The second generation AirTag is the pick for people who want to be guided to the keys rather than just hear a beep. Precision Finding gives step by step directions on iPhone and now on Apple Watch, and upgraded Ultra Wideband and Bluetooth chips let you ping from farther away. Apple says the speaker is 50% louder with a distinctive new chime.

Location can be shared temporarily with trusted contacts, third parties or over 50 airline partners, which helps when a spouse also uses the keys. The tradeoff is that it works only with Apple devices. The listing also gives no battery type, water rating or decibel figure, so we cannot compare it directly with the rated tags here.

Setup is a one-tap pairing with an iPhone or iPad. The bare tag has no hole, so you will need a separate holder to hang it on a key ring. Compared with the Chipolo POP at up to 120 dB, the AirTag offers more precise iPhone finding but no Android support, and against the Qylara 2 pack it is a first-party tag rather than a third-party Find My device.
products.bestFor: iPhone and Apple Watch users who want directions to lost keys.

Speaker is 50% louder with a new chime that is easy to learn
Share location with trusted contacts or airline partners
One-tap setup on iPhone or iPad inside the Find My app
cons: Apple devices only, so no Android phone can use it
Bare tag has no hole, so a holder must be bought

products.name: Chipolo Loop Rechargeable Bluetooth Tracker

specList.label: Battery
specList.value: Rechargeable, up to 1 year per charge

specList.label: Network
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

products.description:
The Chipolo Loop is the rechargeable option in this group, topping up from any USB-C charger and lasting up to a year per charge, according to the listing. A charger is not included, so you will use one you already own. It rings at up to 125 dB, which is the loudest stated figure in this lineup.

Like the POP, it works with iPhone via Apple Find My or Android via Google Find Hub, though one tag runs on one network at a time. The far-away location comes from the global network behind your phone, and the ring helps once you are close. A 2 year warranty with replacement through the seller is listed.

The tradeoff of a sealed rechargeable cell is that it needs a yearly charging habit, and a flat tag on a key ring is easy to forget. The listing gives no water rating, so we do not state one. Compared with the UGREEN FineTrack, which offers a replaceable battery rated for up to 2 years, the Loop never needs a new cell but does need a cable, and at 125 dB it is far louder than the Qylara at 80 to 100 dB.
products.bestFor: People who never want to buy coin cells and want the loudest ring.

Rechargeable over USB-C, so no coin cells to buy or swap

Two year warranty and replacement through the seller
cons: Charger is not included and the tag needs charging yearly
No water resistance rating appears in the listing

products.name: UGREEN FineTrack Air Tracker Tags, 4 Pack, iOS Only

specList.label: Alerts
specList.value: Out of range and Lost Mode

products.description:
The UGREEN FineTrack is the iPhone tag for people who never want to think about batteries. The listing states a replaceable battery that lasts up to 2 years, outperforming standard 1 year trackers, and you can check its level from the Find My app. It is Apple MFi certified, uses end-to-end encryption, and the listing calls it child-safe certified.

It pairs in one tap with an iPhone or iPad and lives in the Items tab. When it moves out of range you get an alert with the last known location, and Lost Mode lets you leave contact details for a finder. Family sharing works through Find My. The listing gives no ring volume or water rating, so we do not claim any.

The 4 pack covers a house key set, a car key, a spare and a bag. Compared with the Qylara 2 pack at a one year cell, the FineTrack goes twice as long between swaps, and unlike the Chipolo Loop it uses a replaceable cell rather than a charger. It is the choice only if everyone in the home has an iPhone.
products.bestFor: iPhone households that want one pack for several key sets and a long battery.

You can check the tag battery level in the Find My app

cons: iPhone and iPad only, so Android is not supported
No ring volume or water rating is given in the listing

products.name: Qylara 2 Pack Bluetooth Tracker, Works with Apple Find My
products.description:
The Qylara is a third-party Find My tracker sold as a 2 pack, which covers a house key set and a car key. It needs iOS 14.6 or later and uses Apple's Find My app with no extra app. The listing states a buzzer of 80 to 100 dB and a Bluetooth range of up to 400 ft.

It carries an IPX4 rating, which handles splashes but not submersion, and a replaceable CR2032 lasting up to a year. Despite the listing calling it a GPS tracking device, it is a Bluetooth tag and relies on nearby Apple devices for far away location, so it is not live GPS. The listing says it works exclusively with Apple devices.

One-tap pairing is the main selling point, and the privacy claim is end-to-end encryption. Compared with the UGREEN FineTrack at up to 2 years of battery, the Qylara needs a new cell about yearly, and against a tag with a full IP67 rating it has only IPX4 splash protection. At 80 to 100 dB it is quieter than the Chipolo POP at up to 120 dB.
products.bestFor: iPhone couples who want two affordable Find My tags in one pack.

IPX4 rating handles rain splashes on a daily key ring

cons: Works only with Apple devices, not Android phones
IPX4 does not cover submersion, only splashes

products.badge: Best for a Shared Family App
products.name: Life360 Tile Bluetooth Tracker, iOS and Android
products.description:
The Life360 Tile is the Bluetooth key finder that runs on its own network and free app rather than Find My or Find Hub. That app works on both iPhone and Android, so mixed households can all use it. You can ring a tag, follow it on a map, or press the tag to ring your phone even when the phone is on silent.

It also includes a discreet SOS alert for notifying loved ones and connects to the Life360 app so family members and tagged items show on one map. The tradeoff is that the listing says nothing about ring volume, water resistance or battery type, so we cannot rank it on those. The family extras are useful only if everyone joins Life360.

Tiles come in 1, 2 and 4 packs, and the tag clips to keys, bags or a water bottle. Compared with the Chipolo POP at up to 120 dB, the Tile offers less hard data but adds the phone finding button, and next to the AirTag it works on Android where the AirTag does not.
products.bestFor: Families who mix iPhone and Android and want one shared app.

Press the tag to ring your phone, even when it is silent
A discreet SOS alert can notify loved ones in a pinch
Sold as 1, 2 or 4 packs so you can start small
cons: No ring volume, water rating or battery detail is listed
Uses the Tile network, not Find My or Find Hub
Family extras only help if everyone uses Life360

buyingCriteria.explanation: A tag only works with the phones its network supports, so this is the first filter. The AirTag, UGREEN FineTrack and Qylara work with iPhone only, the Chipolo POP and Loop use Find My or Find Hub (one network per tag), and the Tile runs on its own app on both phones. A mixed household should not buy iPhone-only tags. Check the listing for the words iOS only before buying a pack.

A loud ring matters when keys are in a pocket or under a pile of mail. The Chipolo Loop claims up to 125 dB, the POP up to 120 dB, the Qylara 80 to 100 dB, and the AirTag has a speaker 50% louder than before but no figure. The Tile and UGREEN FineTrack give no decibel number. Aim for 100 dB or more if hearing is a concern.

There are three styles here. The UGREEN FineTrack has a replaceable cell lasting up to 2 years, the Qylara uses a replaceable CR2032 for about a year, and the Chipolo Loop is rechargeable for up to a year per charge. Replaceable cells avoid needing a cable, while rechargeable tags avoid buying cells. Put the battery date in a phone calendar so a tag does not die unnoticed.

Keys live in rain and bags. The Qylara states IPX4, which handles splashes but not a dunk. The AirTag, Chipolo, Tile and UGREEN listings here give no rating, so we cannot confirm any. If your keys ride in a garden coat, favor a listed rating over a vague claim.

Precision Finding on the AirTag guides you with arrows on iPhone and Apple Watch. The Tile adds a phone finding button and an SOS alert, and the UGREEN adds Lost Mode with out of range alerts. These help only if you use them, so pick the one that matches a real habit. Do not pay for features you will never open.

A tag that cannot attach is useless. The Chipolo POP has a built-in keyring hole, while the AirTag is a bare disc that needs a holder. The Qylara, Tile and UGREEN listings do not describe a hole, so budget for a holder if needed. Check the attachment before buying a multi-pack.

howWeEvaluated.title: Phone and network support
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which phones each tag works with. The AirTag, UGREEN FineTrack and Qylara are iPhone only, the Chipolo POP and Loop work with Find My or Find Hub, and the Tile works on both through its own app. Clear compatibility statements counted most, because a tag you cannot pair is worthless.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sound and finding tools
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how each tag helps once you are close. The Chipolo Loop claims up to 125 dB, the POP 120 dB and the Qylara 80 to 100 dB, while the AirTag adds Precision Finding. All volume figures are manufacturer claims, so we treated them as relative guides.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at listed battery plans and water ratings. The UGREEN FineTrack lists up to 2 years, the Qylara a CR2032 for up to a year with IPX4, and the Loop recharges for up to a year per charge. Where listings are silent, as with the Tile and AirTag, we did not assume a spec.

howWeEvaluated.title: Everyday handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how easily each attaches and sets up. The POP has a built-in keyring hole, the AirTag needs a holder, and the Tile pairs through its own free app. A tag that clips on without accessories scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each pick by what it does best. The POP leads on cross-phone simplicity, the AirTag on iPhone directions, the Loop on volume and charging, the UGREEN FineTrack on battery life, the Qylara on a 2 pack with IPX4 and the Tile on a shared family app. We did not rank on popularity.

faq.q: Which Bluetooth key finder is best overall?
faq.a: For iPhone users who want directions, the AirTag has Precision Finding on iPhone and Apple Watch. For any phone, the Chipolo POP works with Find My or Find Hub and rings up to 120 dB. For a mixed family, the Tile is the most flexible.

faq.q: Do these work with Android phones?
faq.a: The Chipolo POP and Loop work with Google Find Hub, and the Tile has an Android app. The AirTag, UGREEN FineTrack and Qylara are Apple only. A single Chipolo tag runs on one network at a time, so pick Find My or Find Hub when you set it up.

faq.q: Is a Bluetooth key finder the same as GPS?
faq.a: No, this is the most common misconception. A tag rings over Bluetooth when it is close and relies on nearby phones to report where it was last seen. In a quiet area the location can be old. It will not stop a theft.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: The UGREEN FineTrack lists up to 2 years on a replaceable battery, the Qylara a CR2032 for up to a year, and the Chipolo Loop up to a year per charge. The Tile and AirTag listings give no figure here. Set a yearly reminder either way.

The Find My based listings say no extra app, SIM card or subscription is required. The Tile has a free app, though we did not review any paid plans. Check the product page of the Tile before buying if a free-only tool matters to you.

faq.q: Can I use one tag for two sets of keys?
faq.a: Not sensibly, since a tag rings one place. A 2 pack like the Qylara or a 4 pack like the UGREEN FineTrack covers house and car keys separately. That is cheaper than losing a spare set and replacing it.

faq.q: Can someone use a tag to track me?
faq.a: Certified trackers are built so phones warn you about unknown tags moving with you. If you see an unknown tracker alert, follow the prompts on your phone. Never hide a tag on another person or their belongings without their consent.
